newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Paris leads Euro-bourses upwards, dlr steady.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Paris leads Euro-bourses upwards, dlr steady.

text.p: French shares led European equities higher on Thursday, the Paris bourse climbing more than two percent as investors reacted with relief at the makeup of the new left-wing government.

The dollar steadied just below 1.73 marks after news of an unexpected rise in U.S. weekly jobless claims. But the market focus was firmly fixed on Friday's key jobless data for May that will provide pointers to the likely direction of American interest rates.
Soaring platinum and palladium prices, prompted by a severe supply shortage following a halt to Russian exports, dominated precious metals trading.

Palladium fixed in the morning at $235.00 per ounce, its highest level since the twice-daily fix began in 1989, but it later slipped $214.50. Platinum was becalmed at $437 an ounce after a being fixed in the morning at $440, its highest point since September 1995.
Most drama was in Paris, however, where the CAC-40 index surged more three percent at one point to break the 2,700 point barrier, although the froth came off the market in the afternoon.
Traders said investors had been reassured by the make-up of the government, with the appointment of Dominique Strauss-Kahn as Finance Minister seen posing no threat to monetary union.
By 1400 GMT the CAC-40 index was up 64.52 points, or 2.45 percent, at 2,699.89.
Among individual shares, Sanofi jumped 6.59 percent to 550 francs following Wednesday's bullish profit forecast.

Despite lingering concerns over European economic and monetary union (EMU) and Germany's budget problems, Frankfurt share traders voiced relief at an emerging deal to settle Bonn's dispute with the Bundesbank over revaluing the nation's reserves.

"The important thing is that they seem to have found an amicable solution," said Josh Waiblinger, assistant vice president of equities at BHF-Bank, as the DAX index put on a modest 11 point gain in bourse trade. The IBIS DAX was trading nearly 20 points higher in later screen trade.
Airline Deutsche Lufthansa hit a record high of 30.90 marks, a rise of 1.40 marks, with traders citing a positive U.S. research paper. The German carrier closed at 30.80 marks.

London's blue chip FTSE 100 index advanced into positive territory early in the afternoon session as Wall Street opened firm after Wednesday's decline. But after 30 minutes trading, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was just two points up on the plus side.
British shares, down for the last six sessions, met selective buying, traders said, but firm FTSE futures and government bonds lent support.
Activity on both sides of the Atlantic was expected to be restrained ahead of the meeting of the newly-appointed Bank of England policy committee and the U.S. jobs data on Friday.
"I don't think you're going to see too much with this rate uncertainty in front of us," said one dealer.
Back on the foreign exchange market, the dollar was steady around 1.7285 marks and 115.73 yen, but traders were holding their fire before Friday's U.S. jobs figures.
"We're stuck in a range until payrolls," said Keith Edmonds, chief analyst at IBJ International in London.
CURRENCIES AT 1400 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7285 marks and 115.73 yen compared with 1.7310 marks and 116.23 yen in late European trading on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1400 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 10.7 points, or 0.23 percent, at 4,567.8.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 64.52 points, or 2.45 percent, at 2,699.89.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 11.19 points, or 0.31 percent, at 3,673.03. In later screen-based trade, the IBIS DAX was up 18 points at 3,669.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $340.80 against $340.70 in the morning. Platinum was quoted at $437.00, while palladium was $16 lower at $214.50. Silver was four cents firmer at $4.80.
